articles.title: Moradora e mototaxista são baleados durante tiroteio na Ilha do Govern | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher foi atingida no abdômen e homem levou um tiro no ombro; os dois foram levados conscientes para o Hospital Municipal Evandro Freire.
articles.summary: Mulher foi atingida no abdômen e homem levou um tiro no ombro; os dois foram levados conscientes para o Hospital Municipal Evandro Freire.
articles.body:
Moradora e mototaxista são baleados durante tiroteio na Ilha do Governador — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Uma mulher e um mototaxista foram baleados durante uma perseguição policial na noite desta quarta-feira (2), na Ilha do Governador, na Zona Norte do Rio. A mulher foi atingida no abdômen e o homem levou um tiro no tórax. Os dois foram socorridos e levados para o Hospital Municipal Evandro Freire.

Segundo a Polícia Militar, os disparos aconteceram durante uma tentativa de abordagem a um veículo que saía de um dos acessos à comunidade do Dendê . Os ocupantes atiraram contra os policiais e retornaram para dentro da comunidade.

A perseguição ocorreu entre as ruas Tenente Cleto Campelo e Graná.

De acordo com a PM, a mulher estava atrás de uma viatura do Grupamento de Ações Táticas (GAT) quando os disparos foram feitos. Ela foi atingida na região do abdômen .

O mototaxista estava nas proximidades, perto de um estabelecimento comercial, quando foi atingido no tórax.

As duas vítimas foram socorridas pelas equipes do GAT e levadas para o Hospital Municipal Evandro Freire. Segundo a corporação, a princípio, os dois estavam conscientes e sem gravidade aparente .

A ocorrência ainda estava em andamento até a última atualização.

articles.title: Debate Governo do Piauí 2026: Candidatos discutem saúde e água | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro reuniu cinco postulantes e foi marcado por discussões sobre saúde, educação e abastecimento de água.
articles.summary: O debate Governo do Piauí 2026 reuniu cinco candidatos para discutir temas cruciais como saúde digital, educação e o abastecimento de água no semiárido piauiense.
articles.body:
Debate candidatos ao governo do Piauí nesta quarta-feira (2) — Foto: Raissa Morais/Meio News

Cinco candidatos ao Governo do Piauí participaram, na tarde desta quarta-feira (2), do segundo debate das eleições de 2026, promovido pela TV Meio Norte. Estiveram no encontro Rafael Fonteles ( PT ), Joel Rodrigues ( PP ), Dra. Lúcia Santos ( PSDB ), Elizeu Aguiar ( Novo ) e Professor Gisvaldo ( PSOL ). O debate foi dividido em quatro blocos e abordou temas como saúde, educação, meio ambiente, inclusão e abastecimento de água.

O primeiro bloco teve tema livre e perguntas entre os candidatos em rodada dupla. A primeira sorteada foi Dra. Lúcia Santos, que escolheu o governador Rafael Fonteles, candidato à reeleição.

Ao iniciar a pergunta, a candidata abordou os investimentos em saúde digital, mas o tempo destinado à formulação da questão terminou antes que ela concluísse o raciocínio.

Na resposta, Fonteles destacou ações do programa de saúde digital implantado durante sua gestão. Na réplica, Lúcia afirmou que nunca encontrou usuários do serviço e criticou os gastos do programa.

"A saúde digital gasta R$ 15 milhões todo mês do dinheiro da saúde pública, que já tem poucos recursos", afirmou.

A candidata também comparou os investimentos ao custo de construção do Hospital Justino Luz, em Picos, e argumentou que o valor poderia ser utilizado para ampliar consultas presenciais com especialistas.

Na tréplica, Rafael Fonteles defendeu os investimentos realizados na saúde estadual.

"Além do investimento que fizemos na saúde digital, fizemos investimentos em todos os hospitais da rede, inclusive na nova maternidade Evangelina Rosa, no novo Hospital Regional de Picos, nas 16 centrais de exames e na reforma e ampliação de praticamente todos os hospitais da rede", declarou.

O governador também afirmou que o tempo médio de espera por cirurgias eletivas caiu de 464 para 28 dias na rede estadual.

Pessoas com deficiência e neurodivergentes

Em seguida, Fonteles questionou Joel Rodrigues sobre propostas para pessoas com deficiência e neurodivergentes.

Joel citou experiências adotadas quando foi prefeito de Floriano e defendeu a ampliação dos serviços para todos os municípios do estado. O candidato também criticou os gastos do governo com publicidade e afirmou que pretende fortalecer parcerias com prefeituras para expandir a oferta de atendimento.

Na réplica, Fonteles afirmou que o Piauí é referência nacional no atendimento a pessoas com deficiência e disse que pretende ampliar a descentralização dos serviços especializados.

Já na tréplica, Joel voltou a criticar a concentração desses atendimentos em Teresina e defendeu a interiorização da rede.

Na sequência, Joel Rodrigues escolheu Professor Gisvaldo e perguntou sobre propostas para a educação, especialmente voltadas à valorização dos profissionais da área.

Gisvaldo atribuiu os resultados educacionais do estado ao trabalho dos professores e defendeu melhorias para a categoria.

"Nós vamos garantir planos de cargos e carreiras para os servidores da educação pública do estado e da Universidade Estadual do Piauí, cumprindo rigorosamente as promoções e progressões", afirmou.

O candidato também criticou o modelo de ensino integral adotado na rede estadual.

Na réplica, Joel citou problemas de infraestrutura em escolas do interior do estado.

Na tréplica, Gisvaldo afirmou que professores enfrentam jornadas consideradas excessivas e criticou as condições de trabalho oferecidas pelo governo estadual.

Em outro confronto, Professor Gisvaldo questionou Elizeu Aguiar sobre propostas relacionadas ao meio ambiente e criticou mudanças na legislação ambiental discutidas pelo estado.

Elizeu defendeu a preservação ambiental aliada ao desenvolvimento econômico e ao fortalecimento do agronegócio.

"Temos que buscar um equilíbrio para ter um estado que possa se desenvolver dentro do agronegócio e, ao mesmo tempo, preservar aquilo que tem de melhor", disse.

Na réplica, Gisvaldo relacionou a desertificação em Gilbués a atividades agropecuárias e de mineração. Ele também criticou o projeto de Hidrogênio Verde anunciado pelo governo estadual.

Na tréplica, Elizeu voltou a defender leis ambientais mais rígidas e afirmou que é possível conciliar preservação ambiental, geração de empregos e produção agrícola.

Por fim, Elizeu Aguiar perguntou a Dra. Lúcia Santos sobre soluções para a falta de água em municípios do semiárido piauiense.

A candidata afirmou que pretende fiscalizar a prestação do serviço, buscar uma nova concessionária e ampliar a rede de adutoras para levar água às regiões mais afetadas pela estiagem.

"Temos que trazer uma empresa de capital e com adutoras para levar água para todas as regiões, porque, sem água, não temos vida nem desenvolvimento", afirmou.

Na réplica, Elizeu defendeu um projeto para trazer água da Barragem de Sobradinho, na Bahia, com o objetivo de abastecer municípios do semiárido.

Já na tréplica, Lúcia Santos afirmou que pretende realizar estudos técnicos para definir medidas efetivas de enfrentamento à escassez hídrica no estado.

Em seguida, Elizeu Aguiar foi sorteado para perguntar e escolheu Rafael Fonteles. O candidato questionou o governador sobre geração de emprego e renda no estado.

Na resposta, Fonteles citou o problema histórico da falta de abastecimento de água em diversas regiões do Piauí e afirmou que a meta é superar essa deficiência por meio de investimentos municipais, estaduais e federais.

Ao abordar a geração de empregos, o governador destacou o incentivo ao empreendedorismo e o apoio do governo a micro, pequenos e médios empreendedores, por meio de qualificação profissional, acesso ao crédito, redução da burocracia e melhoria da infraestrutura. Ele também prometeu criar 100 mil novas oportunidades de trabalho, emprego e renda.

Na réplica, Elizeu Aguiar afirmou que o estado está endividado e criticou os gastos públicos, especialmente com a estrutura administrativa do governo e o número de cargos e secretarias.

Na tréplica, Fonteles respondeu que o Piauí tem atraído indústrias e outros empreendimentos nos últimos anos devido ao ambiente favorável aos negócios e aos investimentos realizados pela gestão estadual.

Em seguida, Rafael Fonteles questionou Professor Gisvaldo sobre a manutenção do Orçamento Popular caso ele fosse eleito governador.

Gisvaldo criticou os recursos destinados atualmente ao programa e afirmou que é necessário ampliar a participação da população na definição das prioridades do estado.

Na réplica, Fonteles disse concordar com a necessidade de ampliar tanto o orçamento quanto o envolvimento dos cidadãos no processo de decisão.

Na tréplica, Gisvaldo afirmou que o modelo atual não representa uma política séria de participação popular e acusou o governador de priorizar interesses do setor privado.

Demarcação de terras indígenas e quilombolas

Na sequência, Gisvaldo escolheu Joel Rodrigues para responder a uma pergunta sobre a demarcação de terras indígenas e quilombolas afetadas por conflitos fundiários e grilagem no Sul do Piauí.

Joel criticou a política de regularização fundiária adotada pelo governo estadual e também mencionou problemas relacionados ao abastecimento de água em diferentes regiões do estado.

Na réplica, Gisvaldo defendeu o avanço da demarcação de terras indígenas e quilombolas. O candidato criticou a concentração fundiária e afirmou que é necessário garantir segurança jurídica e territorial para essas comunidades.

Joel Rodrigues foi o próximo a perguntar e escolheu Dra. Lúcia Santos. O candidato questionou a adversária sobre a situação dos profissionais da saúde no Piauí.

Na resposta, Lúcia criticou a adoção das Organizações Sociais de Saúde (OSS) na administração de hospitais públicos e defendeu mudanças na gestão da rede estadual.

Na réplica, Joel afirmou que é preciso descentralizar os serviços de saúde e fortalecer os hospitais regionais para ampliar o acesso da população aos atendimentos especializados.

Na tréplica, Lúcia voltou a criticar o programa de saúde digital do governo estadual e disse que a saúde pública do Piauí precisa de melhorias em diferentes áreas.

Em seguida, Dra. Lúcia Santos fez a última pergunta do bloco e escolheu Elizeu Aguiar. A candidata questionou o adversário sobre propostas para o serviço público estadual.

Na resposta, Elizeu criticou a telemedicina e afirmou que pretende encerrar a modalidade caso seja eleito governador. Ele também criticou a terceirização de serviços públicos e defendeu a valorização dos servidores estaduais, citando policiais militares e professores.

Na réplica, Lúcia prometeu realizar concursos públicos, especialmente na área da saúde, e afirmou que pretende recompor o quadro de servidores efetivos do estado.

Na tréplica, Elizeu voltou a criticar o nível de endividamento do estado e cobrou a apresentação de obras e investimentos que, segundo ele, demonstrem a aplicação dos recursos públicos.

No segundo bloco, os candidatos fizeram perguntas entre si sobre temas livres, em rodada dupla e com tempos mais curtos. A ordem das participações foi definida por sorteio. O primeiro candidato sorteado escolheu quem responderia à pergunta inicial.

Em seguida, o candidato que respondeu formulou uma nova pergunta a outro concorrente que ainda não havia participado da rodada, até que todos fossem envolvidos no debate.

Após cada pergunta, os candidatos tiveram direito a réplica e tréplica. Em seguida, o confronto foi ampliado com uma quadrúplica e uma quintúplica, permitindo maior aprofundamento dos temas e mais interação entre os participantes.

O primeiro sorteado do segundo bloco foi Joel Rodrigues, que escolheu Elizeu Aguiar para responder. O candidato perguntou quais seriam as propostas do adversário para reduzir as filas na rede pública de saúde.

Na resposta, Elizeu voltou a criticar a telemedicina adotada pelo governo estadual e prometeu encerrar o modelo caso seja eleito. O candidato também afirmou que pretende extinguir os contratos com Organizações Sociais (OS) na gestão da saúde pública.

"Vamos reformar e ampliar os hospitais regionais. Vamos criar policlínicas em cidades maiores para desafogar esses hospitais regionais. Também vamos criar o pronto-socorro do estado do Piauí, em Teresina, para avançar no atendimento que hoje está concentrado no Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT)", afirmou.

Na réplica, Joel defendeu a realização de uma auditoria na saúde pública estadual para avaliar os gastos e a aplicação dos recursos na área.

Na tréplica, Elizeu voltou a criticar a telemedicina e reforçou a promessa de reformular a estrutura de atendimento da rede estadual.

Na quadrúplica, Joel concentrou suas críticas na necessidade de descentralizar os serviços e reestruturar a rede de saúde para ampliar o acesso da população do interior.

Na quintúplica, Elizeu criticou os recursos destinados pelo governo estadual ao Hospital São Marcos e voltou a questionar a forma como os investimentos em saúde são executados pela atual gestão.

Na sequência, Elizeu Aguiar questionou Rafael Fonteles sobre os empréstimos contratados pelo estado durante sua gestão.

Na resposta, o governador afirmou que o Piauí mantém as contas equilibradas e destacou que o estado está entre os que mais investem proporcionalmente à arrecadação. Segundo ele, a boa situação fiscal permite a contratação de financiamentos para obras e projetos.

Na réplica, Elizeu criticou a quantidade de viagens oficiais realizadas por Fonteles durante o mandato.

Na tréplica, o governador afirmou que participava do debate para defender os resultados de sua gestão e apresentar propostas para um novo mandato.

Na quadrúplica, Elizeu voltou a abordar a falta de abastecimento de água no semiárido e afirmou que possui uma solução para o problema.

Na quintúplica, Fonteles rebateu as críticas e afirmou que Elizeu apoiou, no passado, governos que também não resolveram a questão. O governador acrescentou que houve avanços nos indicadores relacionados ao abastecimento de água durante sua gestão.

Em seguida, Rafael Fonteles perguntou a Dra. Lúcia Santos quais são suas propostas para a população idosa.

A candidata respondeu que pretende investir na melhoria da saúde pública, ampliar a infraestrutura, fortalecer serviços essenciais e criar oportunidades para a inserção de pessoas idosas no mercado de trabalho.

Na réplica, Fonteles afirmou que a população idosa terá prioridade em um eventual novo mandato. O governador disse que pretende integrar ações das áreas de saúde, educação e assistência social para ampliar o atendimento a esse público.

"Quero destacar também que vamos inaugurar em breve o Centro de Geriatria, ali onde funcionava a Maternidade Evangelina Rosa, além de um centro de saúde mental para todas as idades", afirmou.

Na tréplica, Lúcia voltou a criticar a saúde pública estadual e afirmou que filas para atendimento prejudicam pacientes em diferentes regiões do estado.

Na sequência, Dra. Lúcia Santos questionou Professor Gisvaldo sobre suas propostas para combater o feminicídio.

O candidato afirmou que é necessário reforçar as ações de prevenção e enfrentar as causas estruturais da violência contra as mulheres.

"Precisamos combater as raízes reais da violência, e não achar que apenas colocar a viatura na rua vai garantir a vida das mulheres", declarou.

Na réplica, Lúcia afirmou que as mulheres ainda enfrentam dificuldades para ocupar espaços de poder e liderança e defendeu a ampliação de políticas públicas voltadas para a saúde e proteção desse público.

Na tréplica, Gisvaldo disse que é preciso combater a violência de gênero e promover a autonomia das mulheres.

O candidato também defendeu investimentos em geração de renda, empreendedorismo feminino e políticas de trabalho voltadas às mulheres.

"Precisamos romper a cadeia de subordinação das mulheres aos homens", afirmou.

Gisvaldo acrescentou que considera importante ampliar o debate sobre relações de gênero nas escolas estaduais.

Na quadrúplica, Lúcia defendeu a independência financeira das mulheres, suporte emocional às vítimas de violência e maior representatividade feminina nos espaços de decisão.

"Uma mulher tem capacidade e pode, sim, lhe representar", declarou.

Na quintúplica, Gisvaldo voltou a defender a construção de políticas públicas em diálogo com organizações e movimentos de mulheres.

"Dialogar com as mulheres para construir essa política é fundamental", afirmou.

articles.title: Acidente em Grumari: carro cai em ribanceira e deixa ferido no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima foi projetada para fora do veículo e ficou em uma área de pedras de difícil acesso. Bombeiros fizeram resgate por terra, mar e ar.
articles.summary: Acidente em Grumari mobiliza aeronaves e barcos dos bombeiros para socorrer vítima projetada para fora de carro em área de difícil acesso nas pedras.
articles.body:
Bombeiros mobilizaram equipes do Grupo de Operações Especiais (GOESP), guarda-vidas, ambulâncias, embarcações e uma aeronave do Grupamento de Operações Aéreas (GOA) — Foto: Divulgação/CBMERJ

Um carro caiu em uma ribanceira na subida de Grumari, na Zona Sudoeste do Rio, na tarde desta quarta-feira (2). Uma pessoa ficou ferida e foi resgatada por uma aeronave do Corpo de Bombeiros. Segundo a corporação, o estado de saúde da vítima é grave.

O helicóptero levou o motorista para a base do Corpo de Bombeiros na Lagoa. Uma ambulância do quartel do Humaitá aguardava no local para fazer a transferência da vítima para o Hospital Municipal Miguel Couto, na Gávea.

Os bombeiros do quartel do Recreio foram acionados às 14h45 para atender à ocorrência. Militares dos Grupamentos Marítimo (GMAR) e de Operações Especiais (GOESP) também participaram do resgate. Ao todo, duas aeronaves foram utilizadas na operação.

Segundo informações iniciais, a vítima foi projetada para fora do veículo e ficou sobre uma área de pedras, em um ponto de difícil acesso.

articles.title: Morte após diagnóstico de ansiedade: família de Giulia pede justiça | G1
articles.standfirst: Giulia Silva de Araújo morreu horas após buscar duas vezes atendimento no Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles. Polícia investiga o caso.
articles.summary: Família de Giulia Silva de Araújo denuncia negligência e falta de exames após morte por problema cardíaco diagnosticado como crise de ansiedade no Rio.
articles.body:
A família de Giulia Silva de Araújo, que morreu horas após buscar atendimento em hospital e ser liberada sob diagnóstico de crise de ansiedade , segue aguardando esclarecimentos e pede justiça sobre o caso.

Nesta quarta-feira (2), Fabiana Bezerra, irmã de Giulia, conversou com o g1 e revelou que nenhum representante do Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles entrou em contato para ajudar na elucidação do caso. Ela acusa o hospital de negligência.

Fabiana e o advogado da família afirmam que não foram cumpridos todos os protocolos de atendimento no caso.

"Botaram crise de ansiedade para a minha irmã, mesmo ela com sintomas de infarto. Eu sou da área da saúde. Eu percebi que eles não cumpriram os protocolos corretos que deveriam ser feitos, liberaram ela após medicá-la. Enviamos pedidos para esclarecer o fato, mas até agora o hospital não nos procurou, não tivemos nenhum apoio, só nos forneceram os prontuários", comentou Fabiana.

Giulia, que tinha 26 anos e era professora de história, morreu poucas horas depois de receber alta do Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles, em Irajá, Zona Norte do Rio, do dia 28 de agosto. Ela chegou a ser levada para outro hospital em estado grave, mas não resistiu.

O atestado de óbito indicou como causa da morte 'tamponamento cardíaco', que é a pressão exercida no coração pelo sangue ou líquido, que se acumula na membrana de duas camadas que circunda o coração (pericárdio).

O advogado da família, Luan Fernandes, explicou que entre os protocolos deveria constar o exame ecocardiograma.

"A família relatou indícios robustos de negligência médica, em especial, na segunda alta médica dada Giulia. Ela retornou ao hospital relatando novamente um quadro persistente de dor. Ou seja, uma dor forte no peito e não foi feito o exame prescrito pela literatura médica para o caso, que é o ecocardiograma. Ela foi liberada no hospital sem a realização do exame, sem uma investigação mais aprofundada do quadro e, horas depois, Giulia vem a óbito justamente com tamponamento cardíaco, um quadro que seria detectado pelo exame de ecocardiograma", avaliou o advogado.

O g1 procurou a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde do Rio questionando sobre os protocolos adotados e realização de exames complementares. Em nota, a direção do Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles informou que forneceu cópias dos boletins de atendimento à família da paciente e que dados técnicos e assistenciais serão repassados aos órgãos legais e competentes.

Giulia Silva de Araújo — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo a família, Giulia esteve na unidade de saúde duas vezes seguidas, e nas duas ocasiões foi liberada com o mesmo diagnóstico: crise de ansiedade.

Giulia Silva de Araújo morreu horas após buscar duas vezes atendimento no Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles — Foto: Reprodução

"Ela deu entrada no hospital por volta das 8h da manhã com forte dor torácica e muita falta de ar. Mesmo ela relatando tudo isso, liberaram ela porque falaram que ela estava com crise de ansiedade. Por volta das 11h, minha irmã voltou ao mesmo hospital, fizeram alguns exames e deram alta alegando a mesma coisa da ansiedade", explicou Fabiana.

Fabiana contou que conversou com Giulia por telefone e que a irmã havia relatado estar com dores muito fortes e preocupada com seu estado de saúde enquanto esperava por atendimento.

"Nesta segunda vez que Giulia retornou ao hospital, ela estava com tanta falta de ar que não conseguiu nem ficar sentada, e acabou desmaiando na sala de espera. Depois do atendimento, medicaram e liberaram ela para casa", acrescentou.

Ainda de acordo com Fabiana, ao chegar em casa, Giulia teria piorado muito, e acabou sendo levada pela família para outro hospital, em Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense.

"Eu sou enfermeira, estava de plantão quando minha família me ligou dizendo que Giulia já estava quase sem pulso em casa e caída na cama. Saí correndo do trabalho, levamos ela para outro hospital. Lá, tentaram reanimá-la, intubaram minha irmã, mas ela não resistiu", lamentou Fabiana.

O g1 teve acesso aos boletins de atendimento da paciente no Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles. Nos dois documentos, foi informado que a paciente reclamava de dor torácica ao respirar. No entanto, os documentos informavam que todos os exames realizados tinham dado resultados dentro da normalidade.

No segundo boletim de atendimento, consta ainda a informação de que a paciente estava com "100% de saturação em ar ambiente, com ausculta cardíaca e pulmonar sem alterações".

Na terça-feira (1º), a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde do Rio informou que a paciente "foi imediatamente atendida e recebeu todos os cuidados indicados para o seu quadro, o que inclui os exames estabelecidos em protocolo para diagnóstico imediato de quadros cardíacos agudos".

Ainda de acordo com a Secretaria, todos os exames realizados apresentaram resultados dentro dos parâmetros de normalidade: frequência cardíaca, frequência respiratória, pressão arterial, temperatura e saturação de oxigênio. Além disso, informou que a paciente passou por exame de eletrocardiograma, "determinante na detecção de quadros cardíacos de maior gravidade, e o resultado não apresentou qualquer alteração".

A direção do Hospital Municipal Francisco da Silva Telles (HMFST) informa que, na última sexta-feira (28), às 8h32, a paciente Giulia deu entrada na emergência da unidade com relato de dor no peito. Ela foi imediatamente atendida e recebeu todos os cuidados indicados para o seu quadro, o que inclui os exames estabelecidos em protocolo para diagnóstico imediato de quadros cardíacos agudos. Todos esses exames apresentaram resultados dentro dos parâmetros de normalidade: frequência cardíaca, frequência respiratória, pressão arterial, temperatura e saturação de oxigênio. A paciente também passou por exame de eletrocardiograma, determinante na detecção de quadros cardíacos de maior gravidade, e o resultado não apresentou qualquer alteração. Diante da normalidade dos resultados e dos indicadores vitais, foram prescritos medicamentos para os sintomas relatados, e a paciente recebeu alta médica com as devidas orientações.

No mesmo dia, às 11h14, Giulia retornou à unidade e foi mais uma vez atendida imediatamente. Diante da persistência de seus sintomas, a equipe médica repetiu os exames realizados no primeiro atendimento e prescreveu ainda hemograma completo e radiografia do tórax. Também nesta segunda bateria de exames, não foi detectada nenhuma alteração. Ela recebeu no próprio hospital medicação para os sintomas apresentados até então e permaneceu em observação. Às 13h19 foi reavaliada e, como os indicadores vitais permaneceram dentro da normalidade, foi prescrita a alta médica com orientações.

O HMFST lamenta o falecimento de Giulia e ressalta que prestou toda a assistência à paciente de acordo com o quadro clínico apresentado em cada avaliação. A direção da unidade segue à disposição da família para mais esclarecimentos.

Giulia tinha 26 anos e era professora de história no Rio — Foto: Reprodução

A Prefeitura de Duque de Caxias, através da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde e direção do Hospital Municipal Dr Moacyr Rodrigues do Carmo (HMMRC), informou que Giulia deu entrada na unidade no dia 28, às 16h58, já em parada cardiorrespiratória e que a equipe de emergência da unidade seguiu com manobras de ressuscitação cardiopulmonar, sem sucesso.

A direção do HMMRC informou também que a paciente teve o óbito confirmado às 17h25, que foi feito o registro na Delegacia de Polícia e que o corpo foi encaminhado ao IML, para determinar a causa do óbito.

A família registrou boletim de ocorrência na delegacia. A Polícia Civil informou que o caso esta sendo investigado pela 59ª DP (Duque de Caxias) e que diligências estão em andamento para apurar as circunstâncias da morte de Giulia.

articles.title: Women who start common hormone therapy in their 50s may have 23% lower dementia risk
articles.summary: Hormone replacement therapy started between ages 46 and 56 was tied to lower Alzheimer's and dementia risk, a major new UK Biobank study suggests.
articles.body: Women who start hormone replacement therapy (HRT) at a certain age may have a lower dementia risk, a new study suggests. The study, published in Alzheimer’s & Dementia, analyzed UK Biobank data of 183,450 postmenopausal women averaging 60 years of age. The U.K. researchers determined that HRT use was associated with about a 10% lower risk of all-cause dementia and a 16% lower risk of Alzheimer’s disease over a 13-year follow-up period. 'LONGEVITY GENE' MAY PROTECT THE BRAIN FROM ALZHEIMER'S BY BOOSTING DNA REPAIR, STUDY FINDS The association was strongest among women who started the therapy between the ages of 46 and 56. It was also high among those who had undergone surgical menopause. Starting HRT after age 56 was not associated with reduced dementia risk. Dr. Alexa Fiffick, a board-certified family medicine physician and founder of Concierge Medicine of Westlake in Cleveland, Ohio, noted that this was an observational study that can’t show cause and effect. "So, it kind of stays where the data has been for a while — that in certain patients, we have no evidence that it really makes a difference," she told Fox News Digital. 7 NEW DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS REVEALED — INCLUDING ONE MILLIONS STRUGGLE WITH "And, for some patients, such as [those] who go through menopause a little bit younger, whether that's surgically or naturally, or if they have that APOE ε4 genotype that predisposes them to dementia, there may be some benefit." Study limitations The researchers also stated that since this was an observational study, it could not establish that HRT prevents dementia but only showed an association. The study also did not assess any safety outcomes or adverse events related to HRT. Women who use HRT may differ from non-users in other ways that affect dementia risk, such as their overall health, lifestyle or access to healthcare, the researchers noted. Although researchers adjusted for many of these factors, some unmeasured differences could still factor into the lower dementia risk seen among HRT users. The study also did not have detailed information on the types of hormone therapy, the way they were administered or the specific dosages women took. "If you're having symptoms, if you feel not yourself, come in, talk to your doctor, have that conversation." Most of the people in the study were of European ancestry and tended to be better off financially, so the findings may not apply equally to people from other populations. This study alone likely doesn't warrant seeking out HRT just for dementia prevention, Fiffick said. "However, if you're having symptoms, if you feel not yourself, come in, talk to your doctor, have that conversation," she advised. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER There is some data linking menopausal symptoms, such as hot flashes and night sweats, with vascular changes in the brain, the doctor noted. "So, we are very hopeful to see that treating those symptoms may prevent the vascular changes that lead to vascular dementia, but we just don't have that data right now," she said. "So, it's worth the conversation, it's worth bringing up, but I wouldn't go out of your way for just this purpose." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES HRT does carry some known risks and side effects, Fiffick noted. For oral versions of estrogen, there may be an increased risk of blood clots. That risk does not appear to exist for transdermal options, such as patches, gels and creams. Other types of HRT may impact breast activity, overall inflammation, cardiovascular markers and cardiometabolic markers, according to the doctor. "So, it's not one size fits all, and it's really worth an extensive conversation." Looking ahead The U.K. researchers plan to conduct randomized controlled trials to confirm that HRT reduces dementia risk. Future studies will include factors such as estrogen-only versus combined therapy, dosage amounts, administration route, treatment duration, age at the start of therapy, menopause type and potentially APOE genotype. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "I think the more we have studies like this, the more we're going to propel forward the randomized controlled trials to really give women the data they deserve," Fiffick concluded. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Women deserve to have information to use to make decisions about their bodies. So I'm excited to see the trends heading in that direction."

articles.title: Kai Trump reveals emotional college transition, claims she 'hasn't eaten in like three days'
articles.summary: Kai Trump's vlog captures her emotional move to the University of Miami, from tearful goodbyes to strep throat derailing her first week on the golf team.
articles.body: Kai Trump, the 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump, detailed her emotional transition to college life in a video posted to her YouTube channel, capturing everything from early-morning team meetings to an unexpected bout of strep throat during her first week at the University of Miami. The video documents her final days in Jupiter, Florida, before moving into her apartment to join the University of Miami women’s golf team as a freshman. During the drive home after playing a round of golf before her move, Kai spoke about the stress of leaving her home routine behind. KAI TRUMP RECALLS ‘A LOT OF CRYING’ WITH MOM VANESSA BEFORE COLLEGE AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE "I’ve been, like, literally sobbing," she said. "It’s just, like, really sad that I have to say goodbye to, like, everyone today. I’m not, like, a very emotional person at all, so this is, like, really weird for me to cry. "I’m just struggling right now just, like, thinking about it, but, like, I’m excited." Once Kai arrived in Miami, her best friend, Emma, helped her move in and brought along groceries to make sure she was eating during the busy move. KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’ "Emma got me some frozen foods because I haven't eaten in like three days," Kai said in the video. As classes began, the president’s granddaughter chronicled the early start to her athletic and academic responsibilities, noting a 7 a.m. team meeting on her first Monday. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "I’m very tired if you guys cannot tell by my face," she said while getting ready. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The vlog also highlighted her official team gear haul, including Miami-branded apparel and golf equipment, as well as her first team practice. However, her initial week on campus was interrupted when she fell ill shortly after classes began. "I got sick with strep on Wednesday, my first week of school," Kai told viewers later in the vlog. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "I came all the way back to Jupiter because I was so sick. I needed, like, my mom to nurse me back to health." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Trump is the elder daughter of Donald Trump Jr. and his ex-wife, Vanessa Trump. In other recent news involving her family, golfer Tiger Woods arrived alongside Vanessa Trump for Woods' plea conference hearing in a DUI case stemming from a rollover crash in Florida that occurred in March.

articles.title: B&Q and Five Guys among firms which paid staff below minimum wage
articles.summary: More than 600 companies underpaid staff, with £4m returned to workers, according to the government.
articles.body:
DIY store B&Q and the fast food chain Five Guys are among hundreds of UK businesses named by the government for paying staff below the minimum wage.

More than 600 employers were ordered to pay affected workers the outstanding wages, with £4m returned to workers, according to the Department for Business and Trade.

The firms have also been issued penalties worth £7m.

B&Q said the underpayments were unintentional and the result of calculations involving geographical allowances, while Five Guys blamed "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied".

The list of 658 businesses includes shops, restaurants, nurseries, social care providers and a handful of NHS trusts. The government did not say over what time period the underpayments spanned.

Minimum wage is £12.71 for staff aged 21 and over. For 18 to 20 year olds the rate is £10.85, and for under 18s and apprentices it is £8.

B&Q underpaid 4,530 workers a total of more than £456,000, according to the government.

B&Q said in response: "The shortfalls in payments were unintentional. They relate to calculations involving geographical allowances which are paid in addition to minimum hourly rates. All affected colleagues were quickly paid in full in July 2025."

Five Guys, named in the list as owing over £54,000 to 3,699 staff, said "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied" led to its underpayments, which were identified in a review by the HMRC, the UK's revenue and tax authority.

"We worked closely and transparently with HMRC throughout the process and have made all required payments to affected current and former employees," the company said.

St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group failed to pay over £123,000 to 75 workers, according to the list, which also says St George's University Hospitals in Wandsworth, London, underpaid 55 workers.

A spokesman for the two hospital trusts said that "no colleagues were underpaid".

"This relates to a technical compliance issue where part of their salary for a non tax-deductable 'salary sacrifice' (for example, towards childcare) was not counted towards the national minimum wage, even though their gross salary was above the national minimum wage," he said.

A spokesperson said apprentices at Norfolk Community Health and Care NHS Trust were inadvertently underpaid between 2019 and 2023.

They said while their pay met the requirements for their contracted hours, meetings, handovers and time spent changing into uniform hadn't been accounted for, adding the trust has since changed policies and practices.

The other trust named has been contacted for comment.

There were also several nursing homes on the list, and multiple childcare providers.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the government was determined to stamp out the practice of "short-changing your staff".

"The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn't just the right thing to do, it's the smart thing to do," he said.

Kate Dearden, minister for the future of work, said: "Underpaying your staff is illegal, and we will not let workers foot the bill for their boss failing to follow the rules."

"Every employer should check their payroll now and reach out to Acas if they need further support," she added.

The first 10 employers on the government's list, which was sorted by the amount of wages not paid, are:

1. B&Q Ltd, failed to pay £456,934.72 to 4,530 workers.

2. Elysium Healthcare Holdings 3 Ltd, Borehamwood, failed to pay £330,048.81 to 1,095 workers.

3. St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group, failed to pay £123,331.97 to 75 workers.

4. Support Staff Services Limited, Slough, failed to pay £119,715.13 to 323 workers.

5. Forest Holidays Ltd, Moira, failed to pay £100,308.68 to 598 workers.

6. St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London (Wandsworth), failed to pay £77,498.91 to 55 workers.

7. Lanes Group Limited, Leeds, failed to pay £67,893.34 to 297 workers.

8. UK Care Team Ltd, Leicester, LE19, failed to pay £67,082.76 to 99 workers.

9. Five Guys JV Limited, London (Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea), failed to pay £54,642.47 to 3,699 workers.

10. Merlin Cinemas Limited, Redruth, failed to pay £50,198.75 to 181 workers.

The list marks the first "naming round" since the Fair Work Agency was set up in April under the Employment Rights Act.

As well as enforcing the minimum wage, the agency also will soon tackle practices of denying workers holiday and sick pay.

Chair of the agency's advisory board, Matthew Taylor, said naming employers which underpay staff was an important reminder that "paying the minimum wage is not optional - it is the law".

He said: "Most employers want to do the right thing, and we will support them to comply, but those who fall short should expect robust enforcement to protect workers and maintain a fair playing field for responsible businesses."

articles.title: Calor e seca: veja como idosos do DF podem se cuidar para evitar desidratação e outros riscos | G1
articles.standfirst: Por sentirem menos sede com o passar do tempo, idosos são mais vulneráveis à estação. Temporada de seca na capital federal deve se estender até setembro; hidratação é fundamental.
articles.summary: Por sentirem menos sede com o passar do tempo, idosos são mais vulneráveis à estação. Temporada de seca na capital federal deve se estender até setembro; hidratação é fundamental.
articles.body:
Idoso, terceira idade, foto ilustrativa — Foto: Pixabay

Depois dos 60 anos, os cuidados durante o período de seca no Distrito Federal devem ser redobrados: por sentirem menos sede com o passar do tempo, idosos são mais vulneráveis à desidratação . 💧

"O idoso é um desidratado crônico: bebe menos água e não tem a percepção da sede intensa, demoram para perceber a sede", afirma a coordenadora de Geriatria do Hospital Santa Lúcia, a médica Priscilla Mussi.

Segundo a Secretaria de Saúde, os sinais de alerta de desidratação incluem urina escura, boca seca, tontura, câimbras, fraqueza e, em casos mais graves e confusão mental .

O geriatra do Hospital Sírio-Libanês de Brasília , o médico Thiago Póvoa, destaca outros sintomas em idosos.

" Mucosas secas, diminuição de saliva, pele mais ressecada e sonolência excessiva . [...] Idosos mais frágeis, que se comunicam com dificuldade e buscam menos líquido, a orientação é sempre oferecer", afirma o médico.

Além de sintomas físicos, a geriatra Priscilla Mussi destaca que a seca também pode impactar no bem-estar do idoso em relação à disposição e à saúde mental.

"Geralmente, o idoso nesta época de seca fica mais amuado, mais indisposto, mole, porque a pressão baixa mais" , diz a médica.

De acordo com os geriatras e com a Secretaria de Saúde, a vacinação é uma das formas mais eficazes de prevenção contra doenças respiratórias.

No DF, as vacinas da gripe (influenza) e contra pneumonias (antipneumocócica) estão disponíveis em unidades básicas de saúde, confira os locais aqui .

Com base nas entrevistas com os geriatras Thiago Póvoa e Priscilla Mussi, o g1 criou um guia de cuidados com a saúde para idosos durante o período da seca ( veja abaixo ).

Guia de cuidados durante o período da seca para idosos. — Foto: Arte/g1

articles.title: Is sleep tracking making your sleep worse?
articles.summary: The things you're doing to make your sleep better could actually be making your sleep worse.
articles.body:
Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.

Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing". Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.

While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.

That fixation with sleep is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.

So how and why did sleep become so complicated? And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?

The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.

Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.

These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement). Many also give users a "sleep score".

But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.

"There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC. "That's just been created by manufacturers."

Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.

"I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.

Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.

"It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds. "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it."

One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".

In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".

"We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.

Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.

In one study from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.

The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.

The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.

Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.

This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.

"I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.

"I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep. If I'd slept really well, I'd be convinced I'd have to be on top - even though I was tired, I was pushing through things."

Her "obsession", as she describes it, with getting a high sleep score lasted three years, until earlier this year, when she started to notice the watch wasn't reflecting how she'd actually slept.

"I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.

The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.

Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.

"The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC. "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures."

He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.

Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.

"If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds. "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep."

Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason. "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says. "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish."

Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.

Doing light exercise, and eating a "healthy, Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of plant variability".

Above all, keeping it simple - "anything else, you don't need it".

articles.title: The overlooked factor driving the childhood obesity crisis
articles.summary: At a specialist childhood obesity clinic, almost all of the children are not in school. Why?
articles.body:
Ibbie, 16, always struggled with her weight, but it was during the Covid-19 lockdowns that she started eating even more. She was bullied by classmates over her size, and in her first year of secondary school she stopped attending completely.

Away from the routine of the school day, her weight problems worsened.

"When you are at home 24/7 it is very easy to go into the kitchen to get a snack. It's not the same if you are at school," says Ibbie, from Doncaster.

By the age of 12 she weighed nearly 22 stone (140kg) and was diagnosed with liver damage. "I was told that I might need to have a liver transplant if I didn't lose weight. That was scary to hear."

Ibbie's experience is one of the more extreme examples of children living with obesity in the UK – but her story is not unique. She is one of more than 6,000 children who have been treated at a pioneering weight-loss service for the most obese children in the country. These Complications from Excess Weight (CEW) clinics are a network of 39 specialist NHS hubs across England designed to treat severe obesity in children.

Some of the young people treated at the clinics have mental health problems and learning disabilities; others are neurodiverse or autistic.

But there's one characteristic that unites nearly all the children: they do not attend school.

The scientific picture is still emerging, but senior doctors who have spoken to the BBC say that school attendance is emerging as a key, overlooked factor in the battle against childhood obesity.

In the 2000s, when Jamie Oliver was touring British schools for his influential Channel 4 series, it was argued that children were getting fat from buying too many turkey twizzlers at the school canteen.

Now, it's being away from school that seems to be a problem, scientists say.

Childhood obesity has been rising in the UK for decades, and scientists have generally identified a simple culprit: increased consumption of junk food.

But then, in 2020, it became more complicated. While childhood obesity had been rising steadily long before the pandemic, the rates exploded during the lockdowns. The proportion of overweight and obese 10 and 11-year-olds rose from 35% to 41%, with poorer children disproportionately affected.

Although obesity levels have come down since, they have never returned to pre-pandemic levels. The most recent government data shows that one in 10 children starting school in England is obese, but that figure rises to one in five by the time children leave primary school.

Prof Ken Ong, the lead clinician at Cambridge University Hospital's CEW clinic, believes that the current high level of childhood obesity is rooted in the school time that was missed during the pandemic. "We do know that diets got worse. We do know that children did a lot less physical activity. We know that for many children, they became quite isolated being taken out of schools," he says. "I think these are the same factors that are and have been contributing to overweight and obesity."

It's well-documented that even short periods of time out of school, like the summer holidays, can lead to an increase in children's weight. And since the pandemic, fewer British children are attending school altogether. In 2019, about 10% of pupils at English state schools were classed as "persistently absent", meaning they missed at least 10% of classes. Now, it is 18%.

We don't have official, UK-specific data tracking the connection between obesity and school absence, but international research has historically suggested a connection. A meta-analysis published in 2017, which looked at research across seven countries, suggested that an obese child was 54% more likely to be absent from school compared to a child with a healthy weight.

There has been no extensive research in Britain on why school absence might be causing obesity, but doctors who have spoken to the BBC have their theories.

One factor is diet. Since the 2000s - when all four UK governments passed laws to make school lunches healthier - it's become much harder to find high-sugar or high-fat foods in most canteens. At home, those restrictions don't apply. By 2010, a few years after the new laws were introduced, a study from the University of Leeds found that only 1.1% of home-packed lunches met the nutritional requirements that would apply to a meal bought by a child at school.

And a US study from earlier this year found that child obesity rose in states where a universal free school meal programme was withdrawn in 2022 (presumably because it prompted children to eat unhealthy food at home).

"While school food is not as good as it should be, there are some regulations around it," says Keith Godfrey, an epidemiology professor at the University of Southampton. "Whereas in the home environment, it's much more variable in terms of what children receive."

Exercise also matters. A British study from 2014 looked at step counts measured with electronic sensors, and found that most children are more active on school days than weekends.

Dr Catherine Falconer, a leading researcher who has looked at the link between child health and school absence (and who also works for the UK Health Security Agency), says there's "quite strong evidence that going to school has a big impact on health". She adds: "The very act of leaving the house and walking to school is beneficial."

The science is not yet settled, of course, and it can be difficult to disentangle cause from effect. School absence might be driving obesity - but it's also possible that obesity is making children miss school.

And everyone agrees that if school absence is causing obesity, it's just one of many causes. Other factors - like the proliferation of ultra-processed foods - also matter. And there are thousands of home-schooled children in Britain who maintain a perfectly healthy weight.

But scientists who have spoken to the BBC say they are confident that, at least in some cases, school absence is playing a key causal role.

"School attendance is key," says Prof Simon Kenny, NHS England's national clinical director for children and young people, and the man who launched the first CEW clinics in 2021. "I hadn't quite clocked how absent these children are not just from school but from life. You don't see them in the street or youth clubs or sports centres. They are outside of society."

And it can lead to unhappiness. Prof Julian Hamilton-Shield, a consultant paediatrician at the Bristol Royal Hospital for Children, says that the severely obese children he treats are "the most unhappy children I have come across".

Ibbie, the 16-year-old treated at Sheffield's CEW clinic, remembers some dark days. "The bullying got so bad… there was physical bullying as well as verbal," she remembers. "I had suicidal thoughts. It got to the stage where I actually tried to take my own life."

One approach is to send health workers directly into schools to deliver personalised health plans. The CEW clinics have tried just this approach.

Tessa Saunders, a family therapist at Cambridge's CEW clinic, says that schools should in some cases allow children to follow their own diet plans - even if it means breaking school rules. Obese children could be given extra time in the canteen, she says, to help them slow down their eating so their bodies have more time to feel full. And they could be offered an extra snack in the afternoon so they're not tempted to overeat when they get home.

She admits it might "seem weird" if obese children are given more food than other children. But, she says, "there's a reason behind it. It's not the mum trying to make her kid the special one."

She says teachers could also closely monitor the water intake of obese children (sometimes when children think they feel hungry, they are actually thirsty).

"I think in this country we have been focused on school attendance being a school problem," Dr Falconer says. "School absence should be treated as a public health issue."

She also thinks that reversing the decline in school nurses could help spot vulnerable children sooner. "I think there is a real potential around schools being a place you can receive some level of healthcare, whether it's around healthy eating, vaccinations or dental care."

Of course, it takes work to get a child back into school after a long period of absence. Some parents who attend the clinic hope there might be an easier solution to their child's obesity: weight-loss drugs like Mounjaro and Ozempic, known as GLP-1s.

The drugs are only licensed for children aged 12 and over, and they aren't routinely recommended for anyone under 18, under guidelines from the UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence.

Prof Ong says he has encountered parents at his clinic who want access to weight-loss jabs - an easier option, perhaps, than getting a child back into school.

And many doctors see their promise. They point out that obesity in children is a potentially life-threatening condition if left untreated for decades. Prof Julian Hamilton-Shield says he's seen weight-loss drugs have a transformative effect on the self-esteem of severely obese teenagers.

There's a reason child vaccination rates are falling - and it's not social media

Young adults are taking prescription drugs instead of alcohol - and it's dividing experts

A split in the spectrum? The ongoing battle to define autism

Around the same time as she dropped out of school, Ibbie was given GLP-1 injections as part of her treatment at the Sheffield CEW clinic. She was just 12 years old. She lost 10 stone (64kg) and is now much healthier. "It has completely changed my life," she says. "I actually started losing weight before taking the drugs just to prove to myself I could do it. After losing the extra weight I no longer have liver failure, I am no longer prediabetic. I am a lot happier and more confident in myself."

Some parents who are desperate to find a solution to their child's obesity have resorted to buying the drugs privately online. "These parents have the best possible intentions," Prof Hamilton-Shield says, "but I can't advocate for that."

But Prof Ong cautions that weight-loss drugs alone aren't going to offer severely obese children the life-changing health benefits they need.

"Some families see weight-loss medication as a quick fix," he says. "Families who come here have very complex needs and if those aren't addressed then either the weight will come back very quickly, or the medication is papering over the many other needs of these children."

Ultimately, he thinks, it's more important for a child to build a healthy routine - and that means regular attendance at school.

Doctors say that getting obese children back into school could be a key tool to address the childhood obesity crisis. But obstacles remain. The current network of 39 CEW clinics in England reaches just 5% of the obese children that are eligible. The annual cost of treating obesity-related ill health (for all ages) in the NHS is now estimated at £12bn.

Although Ibbie became fitter and healthier, she never did return to school. She says the bullying she received from classmates was so bad she developed symptoms of PTSD. Instead she was home-schooled by her mother, Andrea, with a schedule that included plenty of history field trips. Ibbie's year group took their GCSEs this summer; Ibbie is yet to take them.

But she hasn't given up on education. Inspired by her time at the clinic, she now hopes one day to study healthcare at college. "I just know how life-changing the support in the clinic was for me," she says. "I want to help other people too."

BBC InDepth is the home on the website and app for the best analysis, with fresh perspectives that challenge assumptions and deep reporting on the biggest issues of the day. Emma Barnett and John Simpson bring their pick of the most thought-provoking deep reads and analysis, every Saturday.

articles.title: Police failed me for decades, says survivor of abuse
articles.summary: A woman who was drugged and raped from the age of 15 speaks publicly for the first time about how the police failed her.
articles.body:
A woman who was drugged and raped from the age of 15 has spoken publicly for the first time about police failures she said allowed her abuser to evade justice for more than 30 years.

Tina Duggan sought help from authorities during and after years of abuse by Frederick Allchorne, but says her allegations were not properly investigated.

In 2023, Allchorne was jailed for 22 years after admitting rape, administering drugs with intent, indecent assault and bigamy offences against her.

The Metropolitan Police has since paid her compensation after settling a civil claim over its handling of her original complaint, and acknowledged more should have been done to protect her.

Tina was 15 when she met Allchorne - who is 10 years older - while visiting her father after his release from prison in 1984. She says she was held at a shared house in Sutton, south London, for six years.

Allchorne, 62 when he was sentenced, lived at the house with his brothers. He was already married when he went through a marriage ceremony with Tina, who says she knew nothing of his first wife.

She had her first child at 16 and a second soon after. She says she was extremely vulnerable.

"From the age of 15, after I ate or drank something, I was gone, as if you're going to go into an operation," she said.

"One minute you're there, and next minute you're gone."

At 17, she was taken to A&E at St Helier Hospital in Carshalton at risk of swallowing her tongue, an effect she says was a result of the drugs. A doctor asked what she had taken.

"I didn't even know what he meant by drugs. He had to explain to me in detail that it was a form of tablet," she said.

"From that day to this day, I can't understand why I was sent back to the perpetrator to continue his abuse."

Tina says other men came in and out of the house, and believes one of Allchorne's brothers - now dead - also raped her while she was drugged.

She says she tried to escape but was caught or had nowhere to go, and that her family offered no refuge. Her GP, she says, turned her away several times.

"What more evidence could you want? I felt like they just couldn't be bothered."

In 1991 she reached a women's refuge with her two children and reported Allchorne at Sutton police station.

She says officers told her there was not enough evidence despite her account, her hospital records and indecent photographs taken of her. The case was closed within a fortnight.

In 2009, the Crown Prosecution Service asked Tina for a character statement about Allchorne, then accused of sexually assaulting three children. He was convicted. Tina says the Met still declined to reopen her case.

In 2018, Tina was admitted to hospital after a severe panic attack, which she says began the process of disclosure.

Tina still does not know what drugs she was given. She has complex post-traumatic stress disorder and several physical conditions.

"I've suffered all my life, and I'm still suffering now. I'm haunted by what's happened," she said.

Iftikhar Manzoor of Hudgell Solicitors, who represented her in her civil claim against the Met, said the force's attitude to vulnerable women in the 1990s was very different.

"It's absolutely staggering that Tina was there, crying out for help and assistance, raising her complaints and not being taken seriously, not once but twice," he said.

The claim was brought in negligence and under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, incorporated by the Human Rights Act 1998, which bars inhuman or degrading treatment.

"The civil claim was not only about financial redress," Manzoor said.

"It was also about accountability, some answers." He said time limits created legal obstacles but the Met had agreed to negotiate.

The Met said officers had met Tina and acknowledged "that more should have been done at the time to protect her".

The civil settlement, reached on 19 March, was made without any admission of liability.

A review by the force's Directorate of Professional Standards examined its handling of three reports she made against Allchorne between 1991 and 2018. It found no misconduct by the officers involved.

A spokesperson said there had been "learnings for the Met" and that it had since changed the way it investigates rape and sexual offences, adding: "Every woman and girl in London deserves to feel safe."

The force says arrests and charges for rape in London have more than doubled in the past year.

Now, Tina wants others to come forward, however long ago the abuse took place.

"The perpetrator got punished for what he did, for all the years that he damaged me. So it's never, ever too late. People have got to do the right thing. It's hard but they're not alone," she said.

"I do think people like myself speaking out loud is important. If I can help one person, then it's all been worth it."

For sexual abuse support, visit the BBC Action Line website here .

articles.title: Ismael Galancho, nutricionista y entrenador: "No hace falta llegar a 10.000 pasos; a partir de 7.000 se logra gran parte del beneficio"
articles.standfirst: La cifra de pasos diarios que recomiendan los expertos está por debajo de la popular meta de los 10.000
articles.summary: La cifra de pasos diarios que recomiendan los expertos está por debajo de la popular meta de los 10.000
articles.body: Caminar es una de las formas más sencillas de aumentar la actividad física diaria y no es necesario alcanzar los 10.000 pasos para obtener buena parte de sus beneficios. El nutricionista y entrenador Ismael Galancho ha puesto el foco en una cifra inferior y ha explicado que, a partir de los 7.000 pasos diarios, se consigue "gran parte del beneficio para la salud". La cifra de 10.000 pasos se ha convertido durante años en una referencia habitual para medir la actividad física diaria, especialmente desde la popularización de las pulseras y relojes inteligentes. Sin embargo, la evidencia científica no establece que exista un umbral concreto de 10.000 pasos a partir del cual caminar pase a ser beneficioso. Galancho ha señalado que alcanzar los 7.000 pasos diarios puede ser suficiente para obtener una parte importante de los efectos positivos asociados a caminar. "A partir de los 7.000 pasos diarios se logra gran parte del beneficio para la salud; hacer 10.000 o 12.000 puede sumar, pero mucho menos", ha explicado. La diferencia es importante porque plantea un objetivo más asequible para aquellas personas que llevan una vida sedentaria o que tienen dificultades para incorporar grandes cantidades de ejercicio a su rutina. Una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis publicada en 2025 en The Lancet Public Health analizó 57 estudios que incluían datos de más de 160.000 adultos y examinó la relación entre el número de pasos diarios y diferentes resultados relacionados con la salud. Los investigadores observaron que aumentar el número de pasos estaba asociado con un menor riesgo de mortalidad y de diferentes enfermedades. El análisis identificó los 7.000 pasos diarios como una referencia especialmente relevante, ya que en comparación con caminar unos 2.000 pasos al día se asociaron con reducciones importantes del riesgo en varios indicadores de salud. En el caso de la mortalidad por cualquier causa, los investigadores observaron una asociación con un riesgo aproximadamente un 47% menor al alcanzar los 7.000 pasos frente a los 2.000. Esta cifra, sin embargo, debe interpretarse correctamente: el estudio analiza asociaciones entre actividad física y salud, por lo que no significa que caminar exactamente 7.000 pasos provoque por sí mismo una reducción del 47% de la mortalidad. Además, los beneficios no desaparecen al llegar a esa cifra. Caminar más puede seguir aportando ventajas, aunque el incremento adicional tiende a ser menor. Es decir, pasar de una actividad muy baja a una cantidad moderada de pasos puede tener un impacto mayor que aumentar después desde niveles ya elevados. La recomendación de caminar tampoco significa que exista una cifra mágica que sirva para todas las personas. La cantidad adecuada de actividad física depende de factores como la edad, el estado de salud, la condición física y el resto de actividad que se realice durante el día. De hecho, una de las principales ventajas de caminar es precisamente que puede incorporarse con relativa facilidad a la vida cotidiana. No es necesario realizar una única caminata larga para acumular los pasos. Caminar hasta el trabajo, subir escaleras, desplazarse andando para hacer recados o dar un paseo después de comer son algunas de las formas de incrementar el movimiento diario. La actividad física también puede repartirse en diferentes momentos del día. Para una persona que actualmente camina muy poco, aumentar progresivamente el número de pasos puede ser una estrategia más realista que intentar alcanzar de golpe una cifra elevada. Esto resulta especialmente relevante porque pasar de prácticamente ninguna actividad a caminar con regularidad ya supone un cambio importante. La Organización Mundial de la Salud recomienda que los adultos realicen entre 150 y 300 minutos semanales de actividad física aeróbica moderada, o entre 75 y 150 minutos de actividad intensa, además de actividades de fortalecimiento muscular al menos dos días a la semana.

articles.title: Josh Allen will wear 8 Bills hats designed by Golisano kids. Fans can buy them, too
articles.summary: Josh Allen will wear eight caps designed by Golisano Children's Hospital kids at Bills home games. Proceeds from sales benefit the Patricia Allen Fund.
articles.body:
Josh Allen provided the morose blue potato.

Nine children receiving care at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo turned Allen's famously questionable attempt at drawing the Buffalo Bills logo into eight colorful caps he'll wear before home games this season.

And this time, Bills fans can wear them, too.

New Era released the eight Buffalo Bills hats as part of its 2026 Billustration Collection . Each design is available for $49.99, with proceeds benefiting the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children's Hospital.

Allen will wear a different cap during his tunnel walk before each of the Bills' eight regular-season home games.

Each one features Allen's now-famous hand-drawn Bills logo on the front, with colors and original artwork created by the children stitched throughout the rest of the cap.

Allen and New Era started the Billustration project last season after the Bills quarterback expanded his partnership with the Buffalo-based company.

Allen became the first New Era ambassador to receive an investment stake in the company and was given the title "Director of Billustration." The title was inspired by Allen's attempt to draw the Bills logo from memory.

It wasn't particularly close, but it was memorable.

New Era partnered with patients at what was then Oishei Children's Hospital to create nine one-of-a-kind caps for Allen to wear before home games last season.

Those caps were later signed and auctioned, helping raise $140,230 for the Patricia Allen Fund.

The fund honors Allen's grandmother, Patricia, who died in November 2020. Bills fans responded to her death by donating more than $1 million to the children's hospital, many in $17 increments in honor of Allen's jersey number. The hospital later established the Patricia Allen Fund to support its pediatric critical care team. The fund has raised more than $17 million.

Last year's hats created another problem: Fans wanted them.

New Era and Allen solved that this season by making all eight designs available for purchase.

"I was eager to bring it back for the 2026 season in response to the demand from fans to get their hands on these special caps," Allen said in a news release.

Nobody will confuse them with the Bills' traditional red, white and blue merchandise.

"One of the most special parts of Billustration is seeing the kids' creativity come to life and learning where their inspiration comes from," Danielle Koch, executive director of the New Era Cap Foundation, said in the release. "Their imagination and perspective are incredibly powerful."

What do Josh Allen's 8 Billustration hats look like?

Josh Allen's 8 Bills hats designed by Golisano kids: See every design

Jack's cap features tan, lime green and turquoise panels, a blue brim and a turkey holding a football stitched onto the side. Allen will wear it for the home opener against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 17.

Mason went heavy on red and white and included some of his favorite things, including video games and football.

Charlotte filled her bright pink, turquoise and purple cap with things that make her happy, including rainbows, hearts and flowers. She also incorporated a pair of lungs into the design, representing a major medical challenge she overcame.

Isaac used the colors of a sunset and added a green snapback to represent kidney disease awareness.

Siblings Avery and Amar'e collaborated on a light blue and red design, combining their personalities and love of the Bills into one cap.

Killian's turquoise, tan and green cap includes an axolotl, one of his favorite animals, along with artwork representing two surgeries he underwent.

Caleb created a rainbow unicorn wearing leg braces like his own, while Grace finished the collection with a light blue design featuring a football and other Bills-inspired artwork.

Allen will wear the eight designs during home games against the Lions, Los Angeles Chargers, New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens, Miami Dolphins, Kansas City Chiefs, Chicago Bears and New York Jets.

Where can Bills fans buy Josh Allen's Billustration hats?

The caps are available in three styles: the 9SEVENTY, 59FIFTY and a kids' 9FORTY.

The collection is available through New Era's website, the New Era Buffalo Store, New Era's SoHo flagship store, Highmark Stadium and select retailers.
authors: Ryan Miller, Rochester Democrat and Chronicle
